name: CathNav
full_name: CathNav / Althea I and Althea II: 3-DOF robots for semi-automatic and automatic navigation of steerable EP catheters
group: Ryerson University (now Toronto Metropolitan University; F. Janabi-Sharifi) with University of Waterloo (Y. Ganji) and St. Michael's Hospital (A. N. Cheema)
versions: 2009 IJCARS CathNav, called Althea I by the group (norouzighazbi2021 Sec. 1, ref. 14): Velmex linear stage + two rotary stages, stepper motors, 3 swine; 2021 Artif. Organs Althea II (norouzighazbi2021_design, full): three HerkuleX DRS-0602 smart servos for twist, translation and knob bending (Sec. 2.2.1-2.2.2) on an inclined 3D-printed arm (SLS nylon + FDM) riding a Macron MSA-R6S belt-driven linear actuator (325 mm travel, up to 6230 mm/s), customisable handle parts for other catheters, guidewires and sheaths, magnetic stainless-steel shaft holders, gearbox and external bearings removed, portable, assembly 20 min, five times faster than Althea I, two units can cooperate (Sec. 2.2, Figs. 2-3, 11); the 2024 grip-insert-release follower of the same group is robots_A3 toronto_nazari2024
devices_driven: one bidirectional steerable ablation catheter SteeroCath-T (Boston Scientific): 7 Fr shaft, 8 Fr tip, 110 cm (ganji2009 Sec. System setup); Althea II: EP catheters with rotational knobs, swappable handle holder parts for other handles, guidewires and sheaths (norouzighazbi2021 Sec. 2.2.1)
translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp (2009: Velmex linear stage moves the handle, telescopic tubing keeps the external shaft straight; 2021: belt-driven linear actuator carries the handle holder, norouzighazbi2021 Sec. 2.2.2)
rotation_detail: two rotary stages: one twists the handle, one turns the steering knob
haptics_leader: Novint Falcon 3-D haptic device as input (force feedback N.R.); CathNav GUI
imaging_compat: NDI Aurora EM tracking, two sensors on the distal shaft; fluoroscopy
validation_detail: 3 swine (St. Michael's Hospital vivarium); catheter introduced manually into the right atrium then mounted on the robot; automatic navigation to EM-sensor targets (high RA, tricuspid annulus) (ganji2009 Sec. Experiments setup, Results); Althea II 2021: bench accuracy/repeatability in positioning and velocity modes, comparison with Althea I, cooperative two-robot object manipulation, mitral-valve and clip grasping inside an artificial heart model, image-based visual servoing; no in vivo test (norouzighazbi2021 Sec. 3-4)
key_numbers: mean distance to target 6.53 mm, all trials below 10 mm (ganji2009 Abstract, Results); Althea II: > 90 % accuracy in velocity and positioning modes, about 2.5x more accurate and 6x more repeatable than Althea I (Table 5), cooperative object path error 0.299 mm, YOLO tip detection MSE 0.05 mm (Table 4), assembly 18 / 23 / 17 min by three people (norouzighazbi2021)
